editorial:
Imagine having the perfect life. You graduated from the top college, landed a high-paying bank job, and have a beautiful wife and daughter. Everyone looks at you with jealousy, thinking you have it all. That is exactly where you find Nito Toshimi. But everything flips on its head when he is arrested for killing his own family. The wildest part is his reason for doing it. He tells the court he just wanted more room in his house to store his book collection. It is a strange and creepy setup that makes you wonder what is actually going on inside his head.

What really works here is how the story plays with your mind. You spend most of the movie trying to figure out if the main guy is a monster or if there is a secret he is hiding. The acting is solid and keeps you on edge, even though the pace slows down during the trial scenes. If you like stories that feel like a puzzle, you will love this. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best picture, or just rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night. Adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is also a great move if you love Japanese mysteries.
endingExplained: The big twist is that Nito did not actually kill his family. He spent the whole movie pretending to be a cold-blooded killer to protect someone else and to uncover the real truth. By acting like a villain, he lures the real killer into a trap. The ending reveals that the murder was a setup involving a deeper conspiracy. He finally clears the air, showing that his love for his family was real all along.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological puzzles and unexpected plot twists.
